staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged vulnerable checkout, and the line locations below are grounded in this tree. The sample metadata names vulnerable commit `05f453ec48710066582e3c3f4b71f6a9dc849f2a`, but the prepared workspace used the commit above.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42494318 (gpac): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 9 found by fuzz target fuzz_parse [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42494318
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / reproduction_report.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged 45-byte witness begins with the root-box header `00 00 00 00 61 62 73 74`. In `gf_isom_box_parse_ex()`, the zero root size makes GPAC treat the entire file as one top-level `abst` full box of size 45, and `newBox->size = size - hdr_size` records a 37-byte payload after the 8-byte box header. Because `abst` is registered as a full box, `gf_isom_full_box_read()` consumes the 4-byte version/flags field and reduces the remaining payload to 33. `abst_box_read()` then subtracts its 25 fixed bytes before `movie_identifier`, leaving exactly 8 payload bytes and allocating an 8-byte zeroed `tmp_str` buffer. The string-copy loop writes the remaining bytes `72 6c ff ff 06 ff ff ff` into all 8 positions, finds no `0x00`, and exits only because `tmp_strsize` reaches zero. The vulnerable code checks only `if (i)` and calls `gf_strdup(tmp_str)` without verifying that a terminator was seen, so `strdup` reads past the heap allocation and AddressSanitizer reports the saved heap-buffer-overflow READ. The staged patch adds `zfound` tracking and rejects unterminated strings before `gf_strdup` at this site and the analogous Adobe string loops.

source.description: First project parser statement that consumes attacker-controlled input and materializes the zero-size root sentinel later re-expanded into the `abst` payload length.
source.value_from: The exact staged witness is `gt_results/arvo_42494318/poc` (45 bytes, SHA-256 `5427fb35b042b0e1afb231c4ebfc27d35112fb1cad7a6b3fe55f219845094c0e`). Bytes 0..3 are `00 00 00 00`, so this line reads `size == 0`; bytes 4..7 are `61 62 73 74` (`abst`), and the later root-box special case reinterprets that zero size as the full 45-byte file.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The only post-loop predicate is `if (i)`, so exhausting the field budget with nonzero bytes is treated the same as successfully seeing a NUL terminator.
root_cause.note: The staged patch inserts `if (!zfound) return GF_ISOM_INVALID_FILE;` immediately before this branch, making successful NUL detection an explicit obligation before `gf_strdup`.

sink.description: Project sink matching the saved ASan crash. `STRDUP(str)` assumes `str` is NUL-terminated and reads past the 8-byte `tmp_str` allocation passed from `abst_box_read()`.
sink.note: The saved trace is `__strdup -> gf_strdup -> abst_box_read`, so this wrapper is the first project frame at the crash site.

tainted_value_origin.description: This loop copies witness bytes 37..44 (`72 6c ff ff 06 ff ff ff`) into the 8-byte heap buffer later passed to `gf_strdup`; none of those bytes is `0x00`.

parser_admitted.description: Project dispatch checkpoint into the vulnerable Adobe bootstrap parser. After the root header resolves type `abst`, this dispatch calls `abst_box_read()`.

fine_trace.note: Source. The root box size field comes directly from attacker input. For the staged witness this read yields `size == 0`, which is the sentinel later expanded to the full file length.
The next four header bytes are `61 62 73 74`, so `type == GF_ISOM_BOX_TYPE_ABST` and GPAC selects the Adobe bootstrap parser family for the payload.

Because step 1 produced `size == 0` for a root box, GPAC takes the root-only zero-size path and sets `size` to the full file length. After the 8-byte header, `gf_bs_available(bs)` is 37, so `size` becomes 45.
With a 45-byte root box and an 8-byte box header, the `abst` payload extent recorded in `newBox->size` is 37 bytes. This is the starting remaining size passed into the generic full-box reader.

Because `abst` is registered with `FBOX_DEFINE_S(...)`, the generic full-box reader consumes the 4-byte version/flags field at witness bytes 8..11 and reduces the remaining payload from 37 to 33 before `abst_box_read()` runs.

The fixed bootstrap fields before `movie_identifier` consume bytes 12..36: 4-byte `bootstrapinfo_version`, 1 packed flag byte, 4-byte `time_scale`, 8-byte `current_media_time`, and 8-byte `smpte_time_code_offset`. This reduces `ptr->size` from 33 to 8 and leaves only witness bytes 37..44 for the string field.
The only local size guard for `movie_identifier` requires at least 8 bytes. With `ptr->size == 8`, the witness satisfies this check exactly and the parser continues instead of rejecting the field.

The parser snapshots `tmp_strsize == 8`, allocates an 8-byte heap buffer, and zero-fills it. The ASan allocation stack points back to line 97, confirming that this `tmp_str` buffer is the object later overread by `strdup`.

This loop copies the final 8 payload bytes `72 6c ff ff 06 ff ff ff` into `tmp_str[0..7]`. Every byte is nonzero, so the memset zeros from step 8 are fully overwritten, `i` becomes 8, `tmp_strsize` reaches 0, and the loop exits without ever taking the `if (!tmp_str[i]) break` path.

Root cause. After step 9, `i == 8` and `tmp_strsize == 0`, but this branch tests only whether any bytes were copied. The code does not separately require that a NUL byte was seen, so the exhausted, unterminated buffer still passes.
Because step 10's branch is taken, `abst_box_read()` forwards the unterminated 8-byte heap buffer to `gf_strdup()` as though it were a valid C string.

Sink. `STRDUP(str)` scans memory until it finds a NUL terminator, so passing the 8-byte buffer from step 11 makes `strdup` read into the redzone beyond that allocation. The saved ASan report records `READ of size 9` here with the call chain `__strdup -> gf_strdup -> abst_box_read`.

allocation_context.note: The overread target is the 8-byte `tmp_str` heap allocation created after `ptr->size` was reduced to 8.

format.name: 45-byte root `abst` ISO BMFF full box
format.contract: The verified trigger is the exact 45-byte blob stored in `poc` (SHA-256 `5427fb35b042b0e1afb231c4ebfc27d35112fb1cad7a6b3fe55f219845094c0e`). Bytes 0..3 are `00 00 00 00`, so `gf_isom_box_parse_ex()` takes the root zero-size path and resets `size` to 45. Bytes 4..7 are `61 62 73 74` (`abst`), so the Adobe bootstrap full-box path is selected and `newBox->size` becomes 37. Bytes 8..11 are then consumed by `gf_isom_full_box_read()`, reducing the remaining payload to 33. `abst_box_read()` consumes bytes 12..36 as fixed fields, leaving exactly bytes 37..44 = `72 6c ff ff 06 ff ff ff` for `movie_identifier`. In the vulnerable source those 8 nonzero bytes overwrite the entire zeroed 8-byte `tmp_str` allocation, no terminator is observed, and `gf_strdup(tmp_str)` reproduces the saved ASan heap-buffer-overflow READ. Stage 01 only proves this exact 45-byte witness and observed path; this contract does not generalize to other box sizes, other Adobe string fields, or neighboring byte sequences.
